problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡y-3{x}^{3},\,x{e}^{x}-4x{y}^{3}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the rectangle $-1\le x\le 1,0\le y\le 1.$
worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/2696cdadd3cb020cfbe343b9c372893ac18b63f3548ff71003b7328b19de39d5.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡y-3{x}^{3}$ and $Q(x,y)=x{e}^{x}-4x{y}^{3}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-9{x}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-12x{y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-9{x}^{2}-12x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(-9{x}^{2}-12x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[-3{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]_{-1}^{1}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(-3(1)^{3}-6(1)^{2}{y}^{2})-(-3(-1)^{3}-6(-1)^{2}{y}^{2})]\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-6)\,dy \\  & =-6y\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$
